axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Exa's retrieval and fetching
(web search, web page text, multi-step research Agent) as tools for agents.
axes.runtime:
Mainly the official hosted remote server (https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp, streamable-http);
the repo doubles as an Agent Plugin (agent-plugins.org ecosystem) and a Claude/Codex plugin line.
GitHub 5,162★, last push 2026-10-19 (API verified); GitHub releases are empty,
the release line lives on npm (exa-mcp-server 3.4.2).
axes.local_files: Reads and writes no local files — it outputs search results and web page text (clean markdown).
axes.background: The service lives on Exa's side; session request-response, no background-listening semantics.
axes.tools:
Two tools by default: web_search_exa (search for clean content), web_fetch_exa (read full-page markdown by URL);
optional tools are enabled via the URL parameter ?tools=: web_search_advanced_exa (filters/domains/dates/subpage crawling),
agent_run (Exa Agent multi-step research / list building / structured output).
The repo's skills/ directory ships two Agent Skills, search and exa-agent (loaded when the plugin is installed).
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — each retrieval is independent; multi-step state lives inside the Exa Agent task.
axes.permissions:
**Usable anonymously**: the hosted endpoint accepts anonymous connections with rate limits (official README wording);
higher quotas and Exa Agent require OAuth (recommended, the client pops a login) or an API key
(three ways: ?exaApiKey= parameter / Authorization Bearer / x-api-key).
Purely read-only surface — it cannot write to any system; the risk surface is query content leaving your machine and quota.
axes.fit:
Fits: giving an agent one route with a combined "search + read text" retrieval surface (the two default tools cover it),
zero-barrier onboarding (anonymous works), and the advanced multi-step research Agent surface.
Not a fit: deep site-level crawl orchestration (the crawl/map surface lives in the firecrawl line);
fully offline use (the hosted line needs to reach Exa).

mcp.transport:
**streamable-http** (https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp); the same hosted endpoint when installed via the Agent Plugin / Claude / Codex
plugin lines. Verified: repo README (fetched directly 2026-10-23).
mcp.auth:
Anonymous works (rate-limited); OAuth first (?login or /oauth force the login flow);
API key can go through the ?exaApiKey= query parameter, Authorization Bearer, or the x-api-key header.
mcp.scope: Purely read: search family + web page reading + research Agent. No write surface; no approval needs.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The exact rate limits of the anonymous vs authenticated tiers (the official README only says "rate limits", not verified item by item; per snapshot discipline no numbers are recorded)
- The Exa Agent tool surface and Connect providers details (README points to docs.exa.ai, not verified page by page)
- The compatible-client list of the Agent Plugin ecosystem (README cites agent-plugins.org, not verified item by item)
related: Also an official retrieval+fetch server: Exa defaults to a minimal two tools, Firecrawl is a 27-tool full-family surface.
A retrieval↔fetch division-of-labor contrast: fetch is reference-level single-page reading, Exa packages search and reading into one route.
